summary: Teton County, WY ground-level fire lookout cabin: staffed 1938-1954, burned by the Forest Service in the mid-1970s; listed gone.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone; a Forest Service history says the Forest Service burned it in the mid-1970s.

access.note: The Fall Creek/Munger Mountain area includes hiking, horseback riding, mountain biking and OHV use; no source describes the former summit site.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Lookouts page for Munger Mountain ends with the word Removed, while the Forest Service history says the agency burned the lookouts in the mid-1970s. The story uses the history for how the site ended and the Rex's Fire Lookout Page for the gone status.

notes_for_editor: No source gives a year for the mid-1970s burn, so the destroyed event is recorded with year null; the story says mid-1970s. The Forest Lookouts page is cited for the 1936-1954 record. The Forest Lookouts and FFLA sources name the agency Bridger-Teton National Forest, which matches the brief. The NPS-hosted PDF's publisher was checked on the title page (Bridger-Teton National Forest, 1904-1955; USDA Forest Service). The FS area page does not describe the summit. Search budget: three websearch.py fallback queries, one over the two-per-tower budget; six page reads.
